column1: # The one state-root layout table for the fno state root.
# legacy_name    the file's old name at the top level of the state root.
#                A single `*` makes the row a glob (park rows only); `place()`
# new_relative_path  where the file lives after the migration, relative to
#                the state root. `-` for park rows: their destination is
#                A first segment of `cache` or `logs` names a class: on the
#                default root (~/.fno) it resolves to the cache home or to
#                <state home>/logs. Any other root keeps both inside itself.
# kind           sqlite | anchor | append | overwrite | marker | page | lock | park | dir | keep
#                anchor = the virtual graph.json; its existence probe is the
#                sibling .db. lock = deleted (or parked, for sockets) only
#                after its data file moved and a non-blocking flock succeeds.
#                keep = a name that stays at the top level; legacy and new
#                are the same name, and a `*` makes it a glob.
# owner          daemon (the fno-agent daemon migrates it) | mux (the mux
#                server migrates it at its own start; the daemon skips it).
# Both crates read this file at build time: crates/fno-agent/src/runtime/state_layout.rs
# and crates/fno/src/setup/state_layout.rs. Edit rows here, never in the Rust copies.
# The keep rows at the end are the one closed set of names that may sit at
# the top level. A name no row carries is a new top-level entry: the drift
# reading names it, the write gate warns on it, and `fno doctor lint
# state-roots` fails a new code join that spells it.
# db/ - the graph, event, decision, question and approval stores and their
# pages/ - regenerated renders, folded under cache/pages by the cache-group
# slice; place() reads a straggler at the legacy spelling until it folds.
# logs/ - append-only logs; launchd fds keep writing the renamed inode.
# db/history/ - append-only jsonl journals, plus the durable ledger (one JSON
# doc rewritten per append under /tmp/fno-ledger.lock, so the newer copy wins
# a both-exist merge and the loser parks). The question and decision journals
# stay at the root: the routed store keys their family there, the same anchor
# rule the retired events journal keeps.
# state/ - rewritten runtime state; newer mtime wins.
# The 2026-10-08 batch: the pr-watch, fleet-sweep, provider-runtime,
# failover, health-throttle, recovery-nudge and watchdog-sweep writers, plus
# the three dot-stamps (their dot drops under state/). Python resolves them
# Rust readers resolve through place() on these rows - one table, both
# mux/ - the mux server owns these; it moves them at its own start.
# Fold candidates (ruled set, D2070): one dir row per folder, mapping
# each to itself until its group slice retargets the destination. The mover
# folds a retargeted dir row per child; a self-mapped row declares the
# folder and moves nothing. `worktrees` has no row on purpose: the ruled
# relocation changes the allocation default only (new external worktrees
# land under spaces/worktrees/<repo>/<name>), live checkouts never move
# (lead ruling, 2026-10-16). `sessions` has no row either: the footnote
# harness writes it live (footnote_harness/transcript.rs), so it is a
# folder with a home still to be ruled, never a park entry.
# The wave 2 folders. screens and route-settings drain: a stored question
# row or a registry row may name a child's absolute path. evals keeps its
# claude-config child in place: the sealed eval login is a Keychain item
# keyed by that folder's path. sidecar waits while wizard-lock names a live pid.
# The 2026-10-01 residue batch: an empty dir ensure-global-dir.sh created
# until this table landed (hooks, signals), session scratch (tmp, jobs-tmp),
# and an April foreign-tool drop whose dir carries the legacy brand with a
# leading dot, so its park row is a glob the rename guard can read. None of
# The 2026-11-25 batch: the sentinel and lock of a path migration no code
# calls, the canary's old spelling (it writes state/canary now), and the
# .fno tree a hook created when its cwd was the state root (its events.db
# held 0 rows on the one machine measured).
# Recovery copy rides beside the ledger it recovers (marker: new wins,
# keep - the categories (D2070) plus backups, the park base.
# keep - the named root exceptions (docs/state-root-inventory.md): the
# config contract, operator files, macOS markers,
# the retired journal anchors and the claims cutover guard for old binaries.
# keep - folders whose home waits on the user's folder-set answer (D3581),
# and worktrees, whose live checkouts never move.
